Condition: Two privileged accounts lacked documented evidence of quarterly access review.
Criteria: Privileged accounts should be restricted to approved personnel and periodically reviewed in accordance with the organization's access management requirements.
Risk and Potential Impact: Inappropriate or excessive privileged access may remain undetected and could permit unauthorized access to financial systems or changes to financial data.
Root Cause: Undetermined based on available simulated evidence
Recommendation: Perform and document quarterly privileged access reviews, investigate identified exceptions, and retain evidence of reviewer approval and remediation.

Condition: One quarterly user access review lacked documented application owner sign-off.
Criteria: Application owners are expected to complete and document periodic reviews of user access and approve the review results.
Risk and Potential Impact: Inappropriate user permissions may remain undetected, potentially affecting the confidentiality and integrity of financial reporting systems.
Root Cause: Undetermined based on available simulated evidence
Recommendation: Require application owner sign-off for every scheduled access review and retain evidence of approval and follow-up of identified exceptions.

Condition: Two sampled production changes lacked documented evidence of completed testing before deployment.
Criteria: Production changes should undergo appropriate testing and review before implementation in the production environment.
Risk and Potential Impact: Untested or inadequately tested changes may introduce errors into financial reporting applications and affect the accuracy or completeness of financial data.
Root Cause: Undetermined based on available simulated evidence
Recommendation: Require documented test plans, test results, and appropriate review before production deployment. Define and document controlled exceptions for emergency changes.

Condition: One sampled emergency change lacked documented evidence of retrospective review.
Criteria: Emergency changes should be documented, justified, and reviewed after implementation in accordance with the organization's change management requirements.
Risk and Potential Impact: Changes implemented without appropriate retrospective review may introduce unauthorized or inadequately assessed modifications to financial reporting systems.
Root Cause: Undetermined based on available simulated evidence
Recommendation: Require retrospective review of emergency changes within a defined timeframe, document the review outcome, and escalate overdue reviews to the responsible change management owner.

Finding Title: Incomplete Investigation of Failed Financial Processing Jobs
Condition: Two sampled failed financial processing job executions lacked documented evidence of investigation and resolution.
Criteria: Failed critical financial processing jobs should be monitored, investigated, and resolved, with appropriate documentation retained.
Risk and Potential Impact: Incomplete or failed processing may result in missing, delayed, or inaccurate financial data and could affect financial reporting activities.
Root Cause: Undetermined based on available simulated evidence
Recommendation: Implement documented exception tracking, assign investigation owners, require resolution evidence, and monitor outstanding processing failures through closure.

Condition: One recovery test identified a recovery-time objective failure that remained unresolved at year-end.
Criteria: Critical financial systems should have documented and tested recovery arrangements, and identified recovery weaknesses should be tracked and addressed.
Risk and Potential Impact: Extended system downtime could disrupt financial reporting activities and delay access to critical financial data and systems.
Root Cause: Undetermined based on available simulated evidence
Recommendation: Develop and execute a corrective action plan, assign accountable owners and target dates, address the recovery-time objective gap, and perform a follow-up recovery test.
